production.note: US model years. KBB lists the '2025 Ferrari 12 Cilindri' (coupe and Spider) and no other model year yet. Still on sale. The 12Cilindri Spider is a separate car.

body.note: Front-engined V12 berlinetta; the open 12Cilindri Spider is sold under its own name.

displacementL.note: 6,496 cc. Ferrari: '6496 cm3'; CAR panel: '6496cc V12' (carmag-12cilindri).

aspiration.note: Top Gear: 'this engine continues in production impressively hybrid and turbo-free.'

fuel.note: Footnote: '*With 98 RON petrol'. Top Gear: 'this engine continues in production impressively hybrid and turbo-free' (topgear-12cilindri).

drivetrain.note: CAR panel: 'Transmission: Eight-speed DCT, rear-wheel drive'

transmission.note: Ferrari: '8-speed DCT'. No manual was offered.

powerHp.note: Ferrari's rating is metric: 830 cv x 0.98632 = 818.6, rounded to 819 hp. Quote (Ferrari specification sheet as rehosted by Auto International): "830 cv @ 9250 rpm", footnote '*With 98 RON petrol, including 5 cv dynamic ram effect'. CAR's panel prints '819bhp @ 9250rpm' (carmag-12cilindri); KBB's US listing shows '819 @ 9250 RPM' (kbb-12cilindri). No separate SAE rating published by Ferrari for the US was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS.

weightLb.note: DRY weight: 1,560 kg x 2.20462 = 3,439.2, rounded to 3,439 lb. Quote (Ferrari specification sheet, 12Cilindri Tailor Made release, February 2026): "Dry weight 1560 kg", footnote '**With optional lightweight content'. The sheet does not name the body, but it is the coupe: Ferrari's separate 12Cilindri Spider sheet gives "Dry weight** 1620 kg" (ferrari-12cilindri-spider-spec), and CAR's coupe review states 'sends 1,560kg (dry weight) of Ferrari hurtling towards the horizon' (carmag-12cilindri). No kerb weight was found (Top Gear's review prints none). Step 4 of the weight order (manufacturer dry weight), itself for a car with lightweight options, so a standard car is heavier.
